transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

It depends on what turns out to be wrong. A blockage or split hose is cheap and well worth sorting, but if the motor bearing or fan has gone, a new motor on a 12-year-old vacuum often costs close to a replacement machine, so it's usually only worth it on a higher-end model. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the motor bearing or fan. A whistle or a change in pitch usually means a part-blocked airway. With it switched off, look through the hose, wand and floorhead neck and check the bin inlet. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, is the hose split, or was it all clear?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

I've looked through the hose and I dropped a coin through it, and it goes straight through, so there's no blockage. The suction is weak at both the hose end and at the head. I'm not sure what else to look at, I'm afraid.

The most useful thing to focus on now is the rattly growl itself, because you've already ruled out the bag, filter and hose. The next step below shows you exactly what to do. Switch it on and listen. Has the noise gone, or is it still there?
Yes, the rattly growl is still there when I switch it on. It seems to get rougher after it has been running for a few minutes, and the suction stays weak.

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. A rattle or click is often something caught in the floorhead. Turn it over and remove anything stuck, cut away tangles and check the brush bar (roller) turns freely. Was something caught (and is it clear now), is the bar broken, or was it clean and turning freely?

I'm afraid this Henry is a cylinder type with no powered brush bar in the head, just a plain floor tool, so I don't think there is a roller to check. Is there anything else you would like me to look at?

Check the bin clicks fully home and each filter is seated properly (and dry) — a gap makes it whistle. Was the bin or a filter not seated or clogged (and is it sorted), is a filter damaged, or was everything seated and clean?
I fitted a new genuine bag and a new cloth filter last week, and I believe they are seated correctly. The bin closes properly as far as I can tell, and nothing looks damaged.

Weak suction is nearly always airflow. With it switched off (battery out or unplugged), empty the bin or change the bag, then wash the filters in cold water only and leave them to dry fully — at least 24 hours. A damp filter chokes the airflow too. Was the bin full or a filter clogged (and is it sorted), is a filter damaged, or was it all clean already?

It was all clean already, I'm afraid, as the bag and cloth filter are both new from last week. Something I should have mentioned earlier: after about five minutes it gives off a hot, burning electrical smell, and when I looked at the grille on top in a dim hall I saw sparks flickering inside.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
